What is the IQR?
The interquartile range equals Q3 minus Q1 and describes the spread of the middle fifty percent of sorted data.
Sort the observations
Always arrange data from least to greatest. Quartiles depend on position, not on the order values were written.
Split into halves
For an odd number of values, exclude the overall median from both halves. For an even number, split into equal halves.
Even-count example
Two, four, six, eight, ten, twelve, fourteen, sixteen. Q1 is five; Q3 is thirteen. The IQR is eight.
Odd-count example
One, three, five, seven, nine. Exclude five. Q1 is two, Q3 is eight, and the IQR is six.
Unsorted example
Sort twelve, three, nine, fifteen, six into three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen. The quartiles are four point five and thirteen point five.
Frequency table
Count repeated observations. If one through five each occur twice, Q1 is two and Q3 is four; IQR equals two.
Box plot
The box begins at Q1 and ends at Q3. Its numerical width is the interquartile range.
Transformation rule
Adding a constant shifts both quartiles equally, so the IQR stays the same. Multiplying values by three triples it.
Outlier fences
The upper fence is Q3 plus one point five times IQR. Values beyond it may be outliers.
SAT strategy
When Q1 and Q3 are provided, subtract immediately. For raw values, sort, split, find both half-medians, then subtract.
Final recap
IQR equals Q3 minus Q1. It measures the middle-half spread, not maximum minus minimum. Now practice all eighteen questions.
